questions.q: What is the simplest way to share an OTBI analysis with other users?
options: Email the analysis definition file to each user
Move or copy it from My Folders into a Shared Folder in the catalog, where catalog and security permissions control access
Rebuild it manually for every user who needs it
Sharing is not possible for OTBI analyses
questions.explain: Catalog sharing via Shared Folders, layered on function and data security, is the simplest way to make an analysis available to other users.

questions.q: What direct export formats does OTBI support for one-off distribution of a result?
options: Only RTF
Excel, PDF, and CSV, among others
Only printed hard copy
Only a proprietary OTBI format
questions.explain: OTBI supports exporting a current result to common formats like Excel, PDF, and CSV for one-time distribution.

questions.q: Why do most Fusion Financials implementations route genuinely recurring, scheduled report deliveries through BI Publisher rather than OTBI?
options: OTBI cannot produce any exported output at all
BI Publisher's scheduling, formatting, and delivery options are more mature and more commonly supported for true unattended automation
BI Publisher is a free add-on while OTBI costs extra
Scheduling is not possible anywhere in Oracle Fusion
questions.explain: OTBI is built for interactive, ad hoc exploration; BI Publisher's scheduling capabilities are the more mature fit for unattended, recurring delivery.

questions.q: According to the rule of thumb in this lesson, what should you do when "everyone needs this delivered automatically, every period, without anyone remembering to run it"?
options: Share it via catalog permissions and hope someone opens it
Export it manually from OTBI each period
Build it in BI Publisher
This cannot be accomplished in Oracle Fusion
questions.explain: True unattended, recurring delivery is the scenario the lesson identifies as BI Publisher's job, not OTBI's.

questions.q: If someone just wants to check a live analysis themselves whenever they like, what is the recommended approach?
options: Schedule it to email them a static PDF every hour
Share it via the catalog so they can open the live dashboard or analysis themselves
Export it once and never update it again
Require IT to manually send them a new export daily
questions.explain: When a viewer wants live, self-service access, sharing through the catalog (rather than a static scheduled export) is the better fit.
